PLAYERS TAB (Characters / Archetypes)
What It Does: Define player types and their starting resources.
Grade: B
What Works ✅

Create player types (Warrior, Mage, Rogue, etc.)
Define starting resources (gold: 10, health: 20, cards: 5)
Set victory condition
Define special ability
Set playstyle
AI can auto-generate archetypes

What Needs Rework ⚠️

No resource progression

Only starting values
Can't say "warrior gains 5 health per turn"
Designer Impact: Only works for static games
Fix: Add progression (turn 1, turn 2, turn 3)


No asymmetry validation

Warrior starts with 25 health, Mage with 15
No check if this is balanced
Designer Impact: Might unknowingly break balance
Fix: Show comparative power levels


Special abilities are just text

You type "can attack twice per turn"
No mechanical linking
Can't simulate or test
Designer Impact: Hard to verify it's different
Fix: Link to actual game mechanics


No resource naming validation

You can type "xp" or "experience points" inconsistently
Breaks later calculations
Designer Impact: Game balance checker might fail
Fix: Validate resource names match other data



Designer Verdict: Good for basic setup, lacks balance checking.

Both files are clean. Here's a summary of what was changed and why:

---

### What changed

**1. Complexity Score — content-aware calculation (`blueprint.ts`)**

The old formula only counted *how many* rules/entities existed. The new formula has 6 weighted factors:

| Factor | Max | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Rule count | 20 | Quantity of rules |
| **Rule depth** | **20** | Average word count per rule — a 500-word rule now counts more than a 20-word one |
| **Hard mechanics** | **15** | Keyword scan across rules + description for asymmetric, co-op, legacy, hidden role, etc. — each detected mechanic adds penalty points |
| Entities | 20 | Component variety |
| Player variety | 10 | Number of distinct player archetypes |
| Description depth | 15 | Text length of the game description |

A game with asymmetric rules + 3 legacy rules + average 150 words/rule will now score meaningfully higher than a game with 3 one-line rules.

**2. Game Identity metadata (`overview.tsx`)**

Three new tag-picker sections added to the Game Identity tab (all stored in `overviewMeta` JSONB, no schema change needed):

- **Theme** — single-select chips (Fantasy, Sci-Fi, Historical, Modern, etc.) — violet when active
- **Mechanic types** — multi-select chips (Deck Building, Worker Placement, Area Control, etc.) — sky when active  
- **Target audience** — single-select chips (Kids, Family, Gateway, Expert, etc.) — emerald when active
- **Designer name** + **Publisher / Studio** — two text inputs

**3. Blueprint AI prompt — context-aware (`blueprint.ts`)**

The blueprint prompt now includes all available identity metadata (theme, mechanic types, target audience, elevator pitch, complexity tier, narrative seed, mechanic fingerprint sliders). The instruction explicitly tells the model to use these specifics and avoid generic advice.

Fast to add 50+ components

Clean. Here's a summary of every change made to `entities.tsx`:

---

### What was changed

**1. Duplicate copies all fields** (both `EntityVisualCard` + `EntityListRow`)

Before: only `name`, `type`, `description` were copied. Now duplicating a component also carries over `subtype`, `stats`, `relatedTo`, `color`, and `lore`/`designNotes` — everything the original has, minus its ID.

**2. Property Templates** (inside `EntityProperties`)

A **Templates** button now appears in the property panel header when the component has a known type. Clicking it reveals a panel showing the preset properties for that type:

| Type | Preset properties |
|---|---|
| Enemy / Meeple | Health, Damage, Speed, XP Reward |
| Card | Cost, Power, Defense |
| Item | Weight, Value, Durability |
| Location | Capacity, Danger, Resources |
| Event | Duration, Severity |
| Faction | Strength, Influence, Size |
| Ability | Power, Cost, Cooldown |
| Token / Resource | Value / Quantity + Max |

Properties that already exist on the component are shown struck-through so you don't get duplicates. "Apply missing properties" creates only the ones not already present.

**3. Relationship Picker** (both edit forms)

The free-text "Related to" input is replaced with a structured `RelationshipPicker` component. It:
- Shows existing relationships as removable cyan chip badges
- Lets you optionally pick a relationship verb from a dropdown: `counters`, `requires`, `spawns`, `upgrades`, `drops`, `part-of`, `enables`, `enemy-of`, `ally-of`, `is-a`
- Autocompletes entity names from your project via a native `<datalist>` (typing shows suggestions)
- Stores as `verb:Name, verb:Name` format (backward compatible — untyped entries are just displayed as plain names)

**4. Balance indicator** (inside `EntityProperties`)

When a component has peers of the same type that have numeric stats, an amber panel shows the **stat range across peers** — e.g., `Health: 3–12 (avg 7.5)` for 5 other Enemies. This lets designers instantly spot when a new enemy is way outside the expected stat range without switching to the Balance tab.

All clean. Here's a summary of what was implemented across both tabs:

---

**Tasks Tab — 4 fixes:**

1. **Templates** — "Templates" button opens a panel showing all 6 game design templates (Initial Design, Balance Pass, Playtesting, Rulebook, Component Design, Kickstarter Prep). Clicking "Apply" batch-creates all the template's tasks in Backlog with loading state.

2. **Task linking + dependencies** — The existing `TaskDependencies` component is now wired into the task detail drawer. Every task can link to others with relationship types: *Blocks*, *Relates to*, or *Duplicate of*. Tasks with a "blocks" dependency show a red "blocked by dependency" warning banner in the drawer header.

3. **Changelog / revert** — When you open a task drawer, the current state is snapshotted. If you change status, priority, or description, an amber "Changes since opened" panel appears listing what changed. A **Revert** button sends all three fields back to their original values.

4. **Dependencies** — Covered above. The new "Links & Dependencies" section sits between Subtasks and Comments in the drawer.

---

**Notes Tab — 3 fixes:**

1. **Note linking** — The edit form has a "See Also" multi-picker listing all other notes. Selected notes are stored (via JSON in the `topic` field) and rendered on each card as clickable "See also: Note Name" links.

2. **AI Digest** — "AI Digest" button in the header expands a panel that sends all notes to the AI and creates a pinned blue "AI Digest — May 2" note summarizing: Key Themes, Open Tensions, Next Steps, and Quick Wins.

3. **Flag for later** — `lookAtLater` is now surfaced as a clock-icon toggle in the edit form and as a button on each card. Flagged notes get an amber ring and the header shows a "N flagged" badge.
